A family members' club with thoughtful spaces for parents, babies and children up to 12 years. Dedicated fitness and wellness areas, classes and care for children, and room for the whole family to eat, play and spend time together — set in a 1712 country estate with 4.7 acres and its own lake.

One membership. Zero juggling.

Your week, minus the seventeen tabs.

Right now your Saturday is a soft play booking in one app, a swimming lesson in another, a babysitter on WhatsApp and a cold coffee in the car between Chesham, Amersham and Berkhamsted.

The Bury puts everything inside one gate. Drop the kids at the crash gym or crèche, take a class or clear your inbox in a panelled study, then all meet for lunch by the lake. One subscription. One estate. Your village, rebuilt — in a house that's been here three hundred years.

The Gardens & Lake

The bit no other club can build. Four and a half acres of lawn, mature trees and open water — a jetty to sit on, a meadow to lie in, dens to build and a summer that ends on the grass. Every rival in the Chilterns is a room off a car park; this is an estate.

What The Bury offers parents

A second home — full of life.

Not a place you take the children and endure. A place where your day and theirs happen in the same building, and you stop choosing between them.

The work-from-home day

Working from home — without the four walls.

Some days home is too small, too quiet, or the kids simply need to be with you. The Bury gives you a proper place to work with your child close by.

Take calls in a focus booth. Run meetings in a private room. Step into the garden when you need air, or drop in on them at the crèche. Then back to work — one building, one commute, a full day done without missing them.

Dinner, actually out

An hour at your own table.

Book a table in the Family Kitchen and leave the children in the crèche or the activity centre for an hour. Long enough for a proper meal and an unhurried conversation — close enough that you can see them if you want to.

And if you'd like a glass of wine with it: our valet service will drive you and your car home. Nobody nominates a driver, nobody counts the minutes, nobody sits in a taxi queue at ten at night.

Parking that isn't a problem

Multiple levels of parking on the estate. No circling the Old Town with a toddler asleep in the back, no meter running down while you're mid-coffee.

Something on, every month

A different artistic or musical event every month — recitals on the lawn, exhibitions in the panelled rooms, live music in the hall. A reason to come back that isn't the same reason as last time.

Care you can actually book

Registered crèche hours included in your membership and bookable by the hour — for a work call, a class, a meal, or an afternoon that's yours.

Somewhere the whole family belongs — and nobody is waiting in the car.

Also at The Bury

The things that make a place somewhere you belong.

Beyond the everyday — the occasions, the clubs and the small traditions a family builds around one place.

Birthdays, handled

Private party rooms and the run of the grounds, with the food, the setting up and the clearing away done for you. Bring your people; we'll do the rest.

The Kids' Cinema

Saturday matinées and rainy-afternoon screenings in the house — beanbags, a proper screen, and somewhere warm for you to sit at the back.

A home for NCT & baby groups

Rooms for NCT reunions, baby groups and new-parent meet-ups — with a crèche next door, coffee that isn't from a machine, and nobody minding the noise.

Holiday camps

Half-term and summer camps in the Stables and the grounds, so the holidays stop being a logistics problem.

Seasonal traditions

Easter egg hunts in the walled garden, Halloween in the Stables, carols by the lake at Christmas. The things children remember.

Private hire

Christenings, anniversaries and family gatherings in a listed house with four and a half acres — available to members and non-members alike.

The Grounds

A poetic space for rest, art and music.

Four and a half acres of lawn, water and old trees. Somewhere to sit still and do nothing at all — and somewhere to be moved.

Swim, sauna, repeat
Rest

Water, warmth, and nothing to do

Wild swimming and wood-fired tubs on the bank, a lakeside sauna, and a meadow to lie in. Family hours by day; adults only after six.

Art

A gallery with weather

Sculpture along the water's edge and a seasonal exhibition programme in the panelled rooms — local artists and makers shown first.

Music

Sound that carries over water

Recitals on the lawn, folk and jazz in the hall, and a festival weekend each summer — with selected nights open to the town, not just to members.
